source_title: Universal Verifier: reliable evaluation for browser agents
claim_summary: Vendor post describes a browser-agent task-success verifier co-developed with Microsoft Research and a 246-trajectory human-labelled benchmark (106 trajectories contributed by Browserbase) open-sourced with the paper; claims near-zero false positives vs >=45% (WebVoyager judge) and >=22% (WebJudge)
availability: paper on arXiv (v1 2026-04-05, pre-window); benchmark and verifier code in microsoft/fara (MIT per GitHub API)
limitation: Verifier quality figures are author-reported on an author-built benchmark; no independent replication found; arXiv v1 predates window so only the Browserbase post is in-window

claim_summary: Release notes add global flags for Browserbase session parameters (proxies, advanced stealth, captcha solving, region, keep-alive, session timeout, ad blocking) in remote mode
availability: public GitHub release in MIT-licensed monorepo
limitation: Stealth/captcha flags raise site terms-of-service and access-policy questions; release note is not evidence of correct behaviour

source_title: Benchmarks are marathons, here's how we 5x'd our browser performance
claim_summary: Vendor engineering post claims 5x browser performance improvement (session creation, CDP connection, navigation, teardown) via fewer proxy hops and Go-based CDP proxying; cites third-party ComputeSDK leaderboard
availability: described as completed work; no release date or rollout scope
limitation: No baseline, sample size or before/after values in page text; leaderboard not inspected here; 5x is a vendor claim

source_title: Autobrowse: the Mythos moment for browser agents is here
claim_summary: Vendor describes a self-improving loop that iterates on a live-site task about 3-5 times and emits a reusable SKILL.md plus helper scripts; reports a Craigslist example cut from ~$0.22/~71s to ~$0.12/27s and a case where ~200 lines of deterministic Python beat the agent
availability: availability label not stated; code appears in public browserbase/skills repo (no licence detected by GitHub API)
limitation: Single-task vendor examples; costs exclude human review; skills repo has no detected licence so reuse rights unclear

source_title: Introducing the Session Replay API: Stream browser session replays
claim_summary: Vendor documents GET /v1/sessions/:id/replays and /replays/:pageId returning HLS (fMP4) playlists via pre-signed CDN URLs; up to ten concurrent tabs recorded; recordings stored 31 days
availability: endpoints documented; GA/beta label and plan limits not stated
limitation: Replays may capture sensitive page content; retention and access-control behaviour not independently tested

source_title: Adding foreground tab tracking to the Chrome DevTools Protocol
claim_summary: Browserbase engineer reports an upstream Chromium patch adding embedderData (tabStripIndex, tabActive, tabPinned, tabGroupId) to Target.TargetInfo, landed in Chrome Canary 150.0.7848.0
availability: Canary only at publication; stable-channel status not stated
limitation: Upstream review links in post were not opened in this screen; stable Chrome availability unverified

claim_summary: Release notes add a screenshot option to extract(), ignoreDefaultArgs for local Chrome flags, forwarded model configuration for API-backed sessions and a native clipboard API
availability: MIT; npm 3.5.0 published 2026-06-03
limitation: Release-note entries only; behaviour not exercised

claim_summary: Company announces a one-day Navigate conference in San Francisco on 2026-09-10 and says it will share identity-team research on agent traffic
availability: announced in June for September; no in-window post-event product record found

claim_summary: Release notes add WebMCP support
availability: MIT; npm 3.6.0 published 2026-06-19

source_title: CVE-2026-12823 Browserbase Skills Autobrowse Trace Artifact default permission
claim_summary: CVE record: Browserbase Skills up to 20260526 Autobrowse Trace Artifact Handler had incorrect default permissions (CWE-276/CWE-266); local attack; public PoC referenced; record notes the first version wrongly named Browserbase itself rather than browserbase/skills
availability: third-party CNA record; no vendor advisory found
limitation: CVSS differs by source (CVE record v4.0 4.8 MEDIUM; NVD-displayed v4.0 1.9 LOW; v3.1 3.3 LOW); NVD status Deferred; CVE.org published 2026-06-21T23:45Z vs NVD 2026-06-22T00:16Z

source_title: Harden autobrowse: restrict trace artifacts to owner-only permissions
claim_summary: Merged PR (opened 2026-06-22) writes trace.json/messages.json/summary.md at mode 0600 and run directories at 0700 because traces can hold cookies, auth headers, tokens and screenshots of authenticated pages
availability: merged to main 2026-06-25; repository has no detected licence
limitation: PR does not cite CVE-2026-12823; linkage is the screener's inference from matching component and description; no versioned release tag

claim_summary: browse screenshot now writes a file by default instead of printing base64; a new --base64 flag preserves the old stdout contract
availability: public GitHub release
limitation: Behaviour change can break scripts that parsed previous output; an example of maintenance cost for downstream reusers

claim_summary: Vendor launches a managed browser agent created from a natural-language prompt and run by one API call with async runs, typed result schemas, replay/traces and per-run cost breakdown; states it is generally available on every plan and cites 35M+ sessions/month
availability: vendor-stated GA on every plan with included runs; pricing not on page
limitation: Session volume and customer names are vendor assertions; RuntimeWire 2026-07-06 coverage repeats the announcement without testing

claim_summary: Release notes add context.setDomainPolicy with allowedDomains and blockedDomains lists restricting which domains Stagehand can access
availability: MIT; npm 3.7.0 published 2026-07-13
limitation: Domain policy not tested against prompt-injection or redirect bypass; enforcement scope unverified

source_title: Cut inference costs 30-40% with Model Router
claim_summary: Changelog says setting model to auto selects a model per call and teams typically see 30-40% lower inference cost
availability: changelog entry; plan/model constraints not stated
limitation: Cost saving is an unbenchmarked vendor claim; monetary cost is not energy and routing may change task quality

source_title: Introducing Stagehand v4: The SDK for browser agents.
claim_summary: Vendor launches Stagehand v4 with target management, state and CDP dispatch moved into a browser extension; TS/Python/Go thin clients; breaking API changes (Stagehand.create, async getters, unified Locator); one 50-action Wikipedia run 14.2s vs Playwright 22.7s
availability: npm @browserbasehq/stagehand 4.0.0 published 2026-08-10 under MIT; no GitHub Release object for 4.x found
limitation: Vendor itself calls the benchmark one run; '2x faster / 80% more token efficient' not reproduced; ByteIota 2026-08-14 repeats vendor figures without testing

claim_summary: Changelog says Enterprise customers can send Chrome DevTools Protocol session logs to their own AWS S3 bucket
availability: Enterprise plan only per changelog
limitation: Exported CDP logs may contain sensitive data; retention/encryption obligations shift to the customer

claim_summary: Changelog says users can set cache-hit thresholds for Stagehand results with per-call overrides
availability: changelog entry; relates to v4 server-side cache
limitation: Cache reuse may replay stale actions on changed pages; threshold defaults and correctness not tested

claim_summary: Changelog says webhooks can subscribe to Function events (pending, running, completed, failed)

product: Stagehand v4 code mode / LangChain Deep Agents

availability: getting-started guide linked; release stage not labelled; npm 4.1.0 published 2026-09-09

source_title: Browserbase and Okta: Cross App Access ecosystem brings identity-governed AI to browser agents
claim_summary: Vendor says it joined Okta's Cross App Access ecosystem so enterprise agents can use Browserbase with short-lived, task-scoped, revocable Okta-issued tokens instead of static API keys
availability: 'can now' wording; no GA/preview label
limitation: No Okta-side confirmation located (IT Brief 2026-06-24 coverage of Okta's XAA ecosystem does not mention Browserbase); security statistics in post are third-party survey figures

source_title: How to build frontier RL browser tasks - Browserbase x Hud
claim_summary: Joint post describes four live-website browser tasks with YAML rubrics and answers pinned to stable facts, open-sourced by HUD, and reports per-model scores
